context.why: The package can record an acceptance and say what is outstanding for a person, but no page asks anybody. This story builds the page's view behind templates that already exist and were approved on screen: mvp_compliance/templates/mvp_compliance/agreement.html, the row component templates/cotton/compliance/outstanding.html and static/mvp_compliance/agreement.js. Those three files are FROZEN: do not edit them. Your view must supply exactly the context they read (plan.md, 'What is kept from the prototype'). First you add the batch write record_many() to the model layer, then the view and its route, then the documentation. A failed write (US-2), the 'changed' notice, the query-count guarantee and optional rows (US-3), the configurable default destination and the redirect when nothing is outstanding (US-4), and the reserved slug (US-5) are LATER stories: do not build them.

Repo standards that reviews have missed before: no leading-underscore names anywhere (functions, methods, attributes, modules, template files); line length 88; no compatibility aliases; no test of text content or wording; no test of design preferences (layout, widths, alignment, order of sections, which badge variant); Cotton components and never {% include %} partials
Tests find elements by fixture data, role, id or data- hook. Translated strings are compared with str()
Every user-facing string is wrapped for translation and none says 'compliant', 'compliance' or names a regulation
